issues.what: Both region-OCR calls target the 0.0 s crops E29/E26, which the rationale itself says have "no clearly readable caption" / only "a white vertical mark". Both return 0 text boxes. The crops that actually carry the captions (E27/E30 at 2.2022 s, E28/E31 at 4.5045 s) are never OCR'd, so the report's key text "John Conor", "39 Aug 2045", "CONOR HEWETT", "SEPTEMBER 4, 2021" rests only on the model reading the images by eye.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: In a text-tampering (B family) case it teaches running OCR where there is no text and skipping it where the altered text is, so caption transcriptions go out with no tool backing and misreads would not be caught.
issues.ideal: Run region OCR on the caption-bearing pair E30 (A) and E27 (B), or on E31/E28, and quote the OCR strings in F2, citing the OCR evidence ids.

issues.what: Second OCR on the B 0.0 s crop E26, justified as checking "whether it recognises any text" when the visible content is a "white vertical mark" and E32 has just returned 0 boxes on the matching A crop.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It spends a tool call on a crop the agent already describes as having no text, while the frames with text go unchecked.
issues.ideal: Point this OCR call at E27 (B caption crop at 2.2022 s) instead.

issues.what: compare_media gives the frame-level difference box as "x 0.00–0.60, y 0.77–0.97", but both get_frames crops use box [0.135, 0.745, 0.625, 0.995], so x 0.00–0.135 of the differing area is never looked at. F5 repeats the regional box (x 0.16–0.60) and leaves out the wider frame-level box.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches cropping to the narrower regional box, dropping part of a reported difference area without saying so.
issues.ideal: Crop from x 0.0, or add a limitation that x 0.00–0.135 of the frame-level difference box was not inspected.

issues.what: F1 says "Both ASR results include a question ... and the response 'I'm skydive.'" and treats the transcripts as matching. It never mentions that E35 (B) has an extra segment, "[5.0–5.005 s] Oh, yeah, all of us today.", or that A's and B's segment timings differ (A 1.2 s steps, B 1.0 s steps).
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The task is to compare the two versions, so unmentioned transcript differences, even if they are probably ASR artifacts, teach silently smoothing over modality differences.
issues.ideal: Note the extra 5 ms segment in B and the timing offsets, and call them likely recognition artifacts given the 8/8 sound match.

issues.what: "A and B contain corresponding skydiving-preparation footage ...[E21][E25]". The 'skydiving' part comes from the ASR transcripts (E34/E35, "I'm skydive"), not from the compare image or compare_media result that are cited.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches attaching the nearest evidence ids rather than the ones that support the specific word.
issues.ideal: Cite E34/E35 for the skydiving description, or drop the word and say 'corresponding footage'.

issues.what: The verifier flagged "unsupported_assertion/critical; unsupported_assertion/critical", but the exported REVISED ANSWER is word-for-word identical to the original answer.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: The training target keeps whatever the verifier judged critically unsupported. The likely candidates are image-only details such as "blue-purple banner with a yellow-orange cloud-like graphic" and "B already shows a white vertical stroke", whose records read media_metadata_not_pixels.
issues.ideal: Either cut the flagged image-only details back to what the cited records support, or record that the revise step made no change, so this answer is not exported as 'revised'.

issues.what: T1 copies the full case task verbatim ("Compare the given video A with the candidate video B, and investigate ...") with no decomposition into captions, other regions, audio or face tracks.
issues.why_bad_to_teach: It teaches handing the whole task on unchanged instead of naming the sub-checks. This matters little here because the case is a single comparison.
issues.ideal: Keep one workspace but list the sub-checks: localized region (OCR both sides), the rest of the frame, the audio track, and the face tracks.

good_patterns: Runs compare_media first, then takes matched-time crops of both A and B (0.0 / 2.2 / 4.5 s) before describing the differences; it does not assert 'matches' before the comparison has run.

Numbers are copied correctly from the tool: A 0.2–4.2 s, x 0.16–0.60 y 0.77–0.97, 6.4%, 5 samples, frames 0–149, [0.000, 5.005), peak 6.32%, 8 of 8 windows. The frame-exact segment is kept separate from the sampled region, with its half-open end noted.

Does not adopt the tool's 'typical of AI video editing' hint. It keeps 'B's source identity ... chronological priority' and the editing method as undetermined, and says zero OCR boxes is not proof there is no text.
GIA opens the one report-cited record it was not shown (E30) before finishing.
cannot_judge: Pixel content of E9/E15/E20/E21/E22/E26–E31 (captions, banner colours, 'white vertical stroke', 'orange-and-yellow clothing'). The rendering has no images, so I cannot confirm that A = 'John Conor / 39 Aug 2045' and B = 'CONOR HEWETT / SEPTEMBER 4, 2021' and not the reverse.
Where the '3.2 s' in F1/F2 ('the paired image at 3.2 s') comes from. E21's caption only says 'A 0.2-4.2 s'; it may be printed inside the image.
The E25 limitations were truncated ('Time bounda…[truncated 595 chars]'), so I could not check the source of the '~0.5 s boundary precision' limitation.
What READ_RECORD E30 returned to GIA. The observation is not rendered, and E30 does not appear among the attached images in request_0011.
Which two sentences the verifier flagged as unsupported_assertion/critical.
summary: The trajectory is sound overall: compare_media first, matched crops of A and B, ASR on both tracks, accurate copying of the tool's numbers, and appropriately cautious limitations. The main problem for B-family training is OCR targeting. Both region-OCR calls hit the 0.0 s crops that have no text, while the caption crops (E27/E30, E28/E31) are never OCR'd, so the tampered name/date strings are transcribed by eye only. Smaller issues: part of the frame-level difference box (x 0.00–0.135) was never cropped, B's extra ASR segment goes unmentioned, one citation is mismatched, and the 'revised' answer is unchanged despite two critical verifier flags.
